aspects.says: By default a frame the server can't unpack ends the session and loses the messages behind it; ignore-iso-exceptions keeps a length-prefixed connection reading.
basis: section:3.4 A Frame the Server Can't Unpack Ends the Connection

aspects.says: Each accepted connection holds a session thread until it closes; without a read timeout silently dropped connections fill maxSessions, and then the server refuses new connections while existing ones keep working.
basis: section:3.1 Every Connection Holds a Thread Until It Closes

aspects.says: With a server-socket-factory, bind-address and backlog are ignored; allow and deny still apply.
basis: section:3.6 A TLS Server Checks Client Certificates Only With `serverauth`
aspects.reason: observable only on a listening socket built by a deployed QServer, which the offline runner can't check deterministically

aspects.says: Listeners are asked in order and the first that returns true owns the message: returning true without answering swallows it, answering and returning false gets it answered twice.
basis: section:3.2 The First Listener That Returns `true` Owns the Message
section:3.2.1 Spot the Problem: The Audit Listener

aspects.says: A listener runs on its connection's only reader thread, so slow work in it delays every later message on that connection but not other connections; slow work is handed off.
basis: section:3.3 A Listener Holds Up Its Own Connection

aspects.says: QServer creates each request listener once and every session calls it concurrently, so it keeps no per-message state in fields.
basis: section:3.3 A Listener Holds Up Its Own Connection

aspects.says: A message the server starts goes to the connection the server chooses: QServer's in queue sends to the last connection, so a terminal is addressed through the source it last used, kept per terminal ID.
basis: section:3.5 The Server Picks the Connection for a Message It Starts

aspects.says: clientauth only asks a client for a certificate; the 2.1.7 factory checks it against the keystore only with serverauth, and otherwise accepts any certificate.
basis: section:3.6 A TLS Server Checks Client Certificates Only With `serverauth`

aspects.says: On an unpack failure the channel logs a hex dump of the frame, which ProtectedLogListener does not mask.
basis: section:3.4 A Frame the Server Can't Unpack Ends the Connection
aspects.reason: the dump is written by a deployed channel's logger while it reads a socket; a graded run sees neither, and a practice would only re-read the log the page shows
